fields.text: Who is credited with developing the first commercially practical incandescent light bulb?
fields.explanation: Thomas Edison developed a long-lasting, commercially practical incandescent light bulb in 1879. Earlier inventors made experimental bulbs, but Edison's design was the first practical for everyday use.
fields.hint: This American inventor also founded the company that became General Electric.
fields.whyB: Nikola Tesla is known for alternating current (AC) systems, not the incandescent bulb.
fields.whyC: Alexander Graham Bell is credited with the telephone.
fields.whyD: Guglielmo Marconi is known for radio (wireless telegraphy).
fields.explanationTl: Si Thomas Edison ang gumawa ng unang praktikal at pangmatagalang incandescent light bulb noong 1879. May mga naunang experimental na bombilya, pero kay Edison ang unang pwedeng gamitin araw-araw.
fields.hintTl: Amerikanong imbentor ito na nagtatag din ng kompanyang naging General Electric.

fields.text: Recreational scuba tanks are most commonly filled with:
fields.explanation: Recreational scuba tanks are usually filled with compressed, filtered air, which is about 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen. Pure oxygen becomes toxic under pressure at depth.
fields.hint: Divers breathe basically the same mix of gases we breathe on land, only squeezed into a tank.
fields.whyA: Pure oxygen becomes toxic under the pressure found at diving depths.
fields.whyB: Helium is only mixed into special gases for very deep technical dives; pure helium cannot sustain life.
fields.whyD: Carbon dioxide is a waste gas we exhale; breathing it would be dangerous.
fields.explanationTl: Karaniwang compressed air ang laman ng scuba tank, mga 78% nitrogen at 21% oxygen. Delikado ang pure oxygen kapag malalim na ang dive dahil nagiging toxic ito.
fields.hintTl: Halos pareho lang ito ng hangin na nilalanghap natin sa lupa, pero naka-compress sa tank.
